name: issues.get

description: Read an issue's comment thread. Returns id, author, body, created_at, author_association per comment, oldest-first. author_association is GitHub's role for the commenter on this repo (e.g. OWNER, COLLABORATOR, CONTRIBUTOR, NONE) — use it to tell an authorized operator's comment apart from an arbitrary commenter's; it is null on trackers that don't expose an equivalent (GitLab, Linear, Jira). A `limit` truncates the NEWEST comments off the end, not the oldest — omitting `limit` returns only the oldest 100; hard ceiling 5000.

account.description: Which configured account to use, when more than one is configured for this tracker (e.g. two GitHub accounts). Only needed when `[[scm.rules]]` don't disambiguate.

limit.description: Maximum comments to return. The thread is walked and returned oldest-first, so a `limit` below the thread's true length drops the NEWEST comments, not the oldest. Omitting `limit` returns at most the oldest 100 comments. Hard ceiling: 5000 comments, regardless of `limit`.

description: Record a security finding in this project's findings ledger, so it appears in the control plane rather than only in an external tracker. Use the narrowest scope the evidence supports.

concern_id.description: Catalog concern id, when one applies.

file_path.description: Workspace-relative path, for the code scopes.

rationale.description: Why this is a weakness, and the evidence that establishes it.

references.description: Supporting links — an issue URL, an advisory.

scope.description: What the finding is about. Code scopes: 'line' (needs file_path + line_range), 'file' (needs file_path), 'repo' (the project as a whole). Target scopes, each needing target_ref: 'host' (a machine or IP), 'endpoint' (a service URL), 'resource' (a cloud resource id such as an OCID/ARN/URN).

target_ref.description: The host, endpoint URL, or resource id — required for the target scopes.

name: findings.record
